TXT_CODE_COMMON_SUPPORTS_TAB_AND_CTRL_SH: Supports Tab and Ctrl shortcuts. Disable if compatibility issues occur.
TXT_CODE_COMMON_IF_YOU_ENCOUNTER_ISSUES_: If you encounter issues, it is recommended to disable this feature.
TXT_CODE_COMMON_AUTOMATICALLY_COLORS_OUT: Automatically colors output. Disable if it conflicts with the application's colors.
TXT_CODE_TERMINAL_COLOR_RENDERING_HINT: If the color rendering feature conflicts with the software's built-in color functionality, you can disable this feature.
TXT_CODE_TERMINAL_LINE_ENDING_HINT: If you enter a command and pressing Enter doesn't yield a response, you can try adjusting this option.
TXT_CODE_TERMINAL_LINE_ENDING_PLATFORM_H: If you enter a command and pressing Enter doesn't yield a response, you can try adjusting this option. Windows usually uses CRLF; Linux and macOS use LF.
TXT_CODE_COMMON_CHANGE_THE_ENCODING_IF_T: Change the encoding if terminal output is garbled.
TXT_CODE_TERMINAL_HISTORY_LIMIT_DESC: Maximum size of recent logs shown when opening a terminal. Set to 0 to disable history replay.
TXT_CODE_TERMINAL_SCROLLBACK_DESC: Number of history lines available by scrolling up. Set to 0 to disable scrollback.
TXT_CODE_TERMINAL_FONT_FAMILY_DESC: Use locally installed monospace fonts, with fallback fonts separated by commas.
TXT_CODE_TERMINAL_CTRL_C_PROTECTION_DESC: When enabled, press Ctrl+C twice within the configured interval to send it. When disabled, one press sends it.
TXT_CODE_TERMINAL_CTRL_C_INTERVAL_DESC: Maximum time between two Ctrl+C presses, in milliseconds.
TXT_CODE_TERMINAL_INVALID_SETTINGS: Invalid terminal settings. Check the numeric ranges and font family.
